doc: Haskell's builtin types, and how the symbolic types are spelled in them.

notes.map: An ordered map, so that generated code serializes the same way twice.
notes.bytes: A strict `ByteString`, which travels as base64 text.
notes.any: Held as parsed JSON, since Haskell has no dynamic type of its own.

types.name: Word64
types.doc: An unsigned 64-bit integer. Travels as text, because half its range is outside i64 and JSON numbers cannot be trusted with the rest.

types.name: Integer
types.doc: An integer of unbounded size. Travels as text, because values beyond 64 bits do not fit the wire.

types.name: Float
types.doc: A 32-bit float. Widening to f64 loses nothing; narrowing back does.

types.name: Char
types.doc: A single Unicode scalar value, which travels as a one-character string.
